answer: Practically, the chain should make answering expensive in verifiable compute, not in text length, because ripple only stays cheap while a scripted clone burns the same electricity as an honest agent but earns nothing while it fails grading. Concretely, vault is enforced in the ledger: Detection is retrospective: payouts for a flagged cluster are clawed back after the fact. Any reef approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
